title: A Study to Learn About the Study Medication Called Enfortumab Vedotin in Combination with Pembrolizumab in People with Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer
official: C5701009 - A Phase 3, Open-label, Randomized Study To Evaluate Enfortumab Vedotin in Combination with Pembrolizumab in Adult participants with Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer Who Are Ineligible for or have elected not to undergo cystectomy
summary:
Main objective: To compare BI-EFS between Arm A (EV+P) and Arm B (cCRT)
To compare OS between Arm A (EV+P) and Arm B (cCRT)

interventions.name: Padcev 30 mg powder for concentrate for solution for infusion
KEYTRUDA 25 mg/mL concentrate for solution for infusion.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. 18 years of age or older (or the minimum age of consent in accordance with local regulations) at screening. Refer to Appendix 4 for reproductive criteria for male (Section 10.4.1) and female (Section 10.4.2) participants.
2. 2. Have a histologically confirmed initial diagnosis of MIBC (clinical T2-T4a N0M0 with predominant (≥50%) urothelial carcinoma by BICR and have not been previously treated with systemic therapy or radiotherapy for bladder cancer. Have a maxTURBT 60 days (+ 14 days) prior to randomization Note: For confirmation of T2-T4a disease, TURBT biopsy samples must include detrusor muscle, without which tumor samples will not be evaluated by central vendor. Participants must undergo radiological staging within 4 weeks of randomization. Staging will be determined by central pathology and radiology assessments for the purpose of study eligibility and stratification. Participants should have no hydronephrosis or unilateral hydronephrosis (if unilateral hydronephrosis, kidney function must not meet criteria specified in exclusion criterion 15).
3. 3. Participants must be eligible for and agree to receive chemoradiotherapy and one of the protocol-specified radiosensitizing chemotherapy regimens.
4. 4. Resolution of acute effects of any prior therapy to NCI CTCAE Grade ≤1 prior to randomization (except for AEs not constituting a safety risk in the investigator’s judgment).
5. 5. Participants should be fit for systemic therapy per investigator’s judgement and elect bladder preservation, including participants who are ineligible for or have elected not to undergo cystectomy. Reasons for ineligibility or refusal of cystectomy should be discussed with the participant as part of the informed consent process and should be captured on the appropriate CRF.
6. 6. ECOG PS 0-2
7. 7. Participants must provide written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. 01. Advanced or metastatic disease (N+ or M1), diffuse or multifocal CIS (≥4 distinct CIS lesions in the bladder), urothelial carcinoma or histological variant at any site outside of the urinary bladder within the previous 24 months prior to randomization except Ta/T1/CIS of the upper urinary tract including renal pelvis and ureter if the participant had undergone complete nephroureterectomy.
2. 18. Meet any of the following criteria regarding past or current infections: a. Has a known history of HIV infection with CD4+ T-cell (CD4+) <350 cells/ul or AIDS-defining opportunistic infections within the past 12 months prior to randomization. Testing is not required unless mandated by local health authorities. b. Participants with known active hepatitis B (defined as HBsAg reactive) who meet criteria for antiviral therapy but have not initiated treatment prior to receiving study therapy, or who are unable to maintain antiviral therapy during the course of the study, will be excluded; participants with known uncontrolled active hepatitis C virus (defined as HCV RNA [qualitative] detected) infection. Testing for hepatitis B and hepatitis C is required if mandated by country health authority. c. Note: Participants who have been curatively treated for hepatitis C infection are permitted if they have documented sustained virologic response of 12 weeks. d. Participants with active tuberculosis. e. Currently receiving systemic antimicrobial treatment for active infection (viral except HBV and HCV, bacterial, or fungal) at the time of randomization. Routine antimicrobial prophylaxis is permitted.
3. 07. Participants with a history of ILD, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organizing pneumonia, drug-induced pneumonitis, idiopathic pneumonitis, or evidence of active pneumonitis on screening chest CT scan.
4. 08. Known genetic disorders associated with radiosensitivity (eg, ataxia telangiectasia, Nijmegen breakage syndrome, Fanconi syndrome).
5. 09. History of autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in the past 2 years prior to randomization (ie, with use of disease modifying agents, corticosteroid, or immunosuppressive drugs). • Replacement therapy (eg, thyroxine, insulin, physiologic corticosteroid replacement therapy for adrenal or pituitary insufficiency) is not considered a form of systemic treatment and is allowed. • Brief (7 days) use of systemic corticosteroid is allowed when use is considered SOC. • Participants with vitiligo, psoriasis, T1DM, hypothyroidism, or resolved childhood asthma/atopy will not be excluded. • Participants requiring intermittent use of bronchodilators, inhaled corticosteroids, or local steroid injections will not be excluded. • Participants with hypothyroidism that is stable with hormone replacement or Sjogren’s syndrome will not be excluded.
6. 13. Participants who have received major surgery within 4 weeks prior to randomization. Participant must have recovered adequately from complications from the intervention prior to starting study intervention. Note: TURBT, cystoscopy, and nephrostomy tubes are not considered major surgery. Participants having an implantable port placed can enter the study on the same day the port is placed, assuming no complications have occurred, and the port is functioning normally. Minor surgical procedures require at least 1-week period prior to randomization.
7. 14. Previous administration of an investigational product (drug or vaccine) for any other indication within 30 days or 5 half-lives preceding the first dose of study intervention used in this study (whichever is longer). Participation in other studies involving study intervention for any other indication within 4 weeks prior to randomization. A participant may be eligible if they are in the follow-up phase of an investigational study for any other indication as long as they have not received treatment in that study for at least 4 weeks after the last dose of the previous investigational agent.
8. 10. Has received any prior systemic treatment, chemoradiation, and/or radiation for MIBC or NMIBC. Note: Prior treatment for NMIBC with intravesical instillation therapy such as BCG or intravesical chemotherapy is permitted. Prior systemic treatment (including, but not limited to, anti-PD 1/L1 treatment with pembrolizumab, etc) received for NMIBC is not permitted.
9. 11. Has received any of the following therapies for any indication prior to randomization, as defined below: a. Participants who have previously received EV or other MMAE-based ADCs. b. Participants who have received prior treatment with a PD-(L)-1 inhibitor for any malignancy, including earlier stage UC, defined as a PD-1 inhibitor or PD-L1 inhibitor (including, but not limited to, atezolizumab, pembrolizumab, nivolumab, durvalumab, or avelumab). c. Participants who have previously received any prior treatment with an agent directed to another stimulatory or co inhibitory T-cell receptor (including but not limited to CD137 agonists, CTLA-4 inhibitors, or OX-30 agonists). d. Participants who have received a prior allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplant. e. Participants who have received prior pelvic radiation for any reason.
10. 12. Use of any prohibited concomitant medication(s) within 30 days prior to the first dose of study intervention or unwillingness or inability to use a required concomitant medication(s). Refer to Section 6.9.2.
11. 19. Baseline standard 12 lead ECG that demonstrates clinically relevant abnormalities that may affect participant safety or interpretation of study results (including, but not limited to, baseline QTcF >470 ms, complete LBBB, signs of an acute or indeterminate age myocardial infarction, ST segment and/or T wave changes suggestive of active myocardial ischemia, second- or third- degree AV block, or serious bradyarrhythmias or tachyarrhythmias). If QTcF exceeds 470 ms, or QRS complex exceeds 120 ms, the ECG should be repeated twice and the average of the 3 QTcF or QRS complex values should be used to determine the participant’s eligibility. Computer-interpreted ECGs with abnormal findings should be overread by an investigator physician experienced in reading ECGs before excluding participants.
12. 02. Inadequate bladder function as assessed by a physician defined by frequency of small amounts of urine (<30 mL), urinary incontinence, or requires self-catheterization or a permanent indwelling catheter.
13. 20. Any of the following in the previous 6 months prior to randomization: myocardial infarction, long QT syndrome, Torsade de Pointes, clinically important atrial or ventricular arrhythmias (including sustained ventricular tachyarrhythmia and ventricular fibrillation), serious conduction system abnormalities (eg, bifascicular block defined as right bundle branch and left anterior or posterior hemiblock, 3rd degree AV block), unstable angina, coronary/peripheral artery bypass graft, symptomatic CHF, NYHA Class III or IV, cerebrovascular accident, transient ischemic attack, symptomatic pulmonary embolism, and/or other clinical significant episode of thrombo-embolic disease. Ongoing cardiac dysrhythmias of NCI CTCAE ≥ Grade 2, atrial fibrillation of any grade (≥ Grade 2 in the case of asymptomatic lone atrial fibrillation). If a participant has a cardiac rhythm device/pacemaker placed and QTcF >470 ms, the participant may be considered eligible. Participants with cardiac rhythm device/pacemaker must be discussed in detail with the sponsor to judge eligibility.
14. 21. Investigator site staff directly involved in the conduct of the study and their family members, site staff otherwise supervised by the investigator, and sponsor and sponsor delegate employees directly involved in the conduct of the study and their family members.
15. 03. Participants with any other active malignancy within 3 years prior to randomization, except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, or CIS (eg, breast carcinoma, cervical cancer) who have undergone potentially curative therapy, Bowen’s disease, or low-grade (Gleason 6 or below) prostate cancer on surveillance without any plans for treatment intervention (eg, surgery, radiation, or castration).
16. 04. Known or suspected hypersensitivity to EV and/or pembrolizumab. Participants with known or severe (≥ Grade 3) hypersensitivity to any EV excipient contained in the drug formulation of EV (including histidine, trehalose dihydrate, and polysorbate 20). Participants with known severe (≥ Grade 3) hypersensitivity to any pembrolizumab excipient contained in the drug formulations of pembrolizumab. Participants with known severe (≥ Grade 3) hypersensitivity to platinum-containing agents, fluorouracil or gemcitabine selected by the investigator for study intervention.
17. 05. Have any of the following current medical conditions as defined below: a. Participants with uncontrolled diabetes. Uncontrolled diabetes is defined as HbA1c ≥8% or HbA1c 7% to <8% with associated diabetes symptoms (polyuria or polydipsia) that are not otherwise explained. b. Participants with ongoing sensory or motor neuropathy Grade 2 or higher. c. Participants with active keratitis or corneal ulcerations. Participants with superficial punctate keratitis are allowed if the disorder is being adequately treated in the opinion of the investigator. d. Any medical or psychiatric condition including any active suicidal ideation in the past year or suicidal behavior in the past 5 years or laboratory abnormality that may increase the risk of study participation or, in the investigator’s judgment, make the participant inappropriate for the study.
18. 06. Has a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy (in dosing exceeding 10 mg daily of prednisone equivalent) or any other form of immunosuppressive therapy within 7 days prior the first dose of study intervention. Inhaled or topical steroids are permitted in the absence of active autoimmune disease. Physiologic replacement doses of corticosteroids are permitted for participants with adrenal insufficiency.
19. 15. Renal impairment as defined by CrCl <30 mL/min, which may be confirmed by a single repeat test, if necessary. CrCl should be calculated using one of the following methods: Cockroft-Gault method, MDRD (see Section 10.2.1), or a 24-hour urine collection. The same method for CrCl calculation should be used consistently for a participant over the course of the study. eGFR can also be used in place of CrCl.
20. 16. Hepatic dysfunction defined as having any 1 of the following, which may be confirmed by a single repeat test, if necessary: Total bilirubin >1.5 × ULN OR direct bilirubin > ULN for participants with total bilirubin levels >1.5 × ULN (except for Gilbert’s syndrome, direct bilirubin >3 × ULN is exclusionary) AST >2.5 × ULN ALT >2.5 × ULN
21. 17. Hematologic abnormalities defined as any 1 of the following, which may be confirmed by a single repeat test, if necessary: ANC <1500/μL Platelets <100,000/μL Hemoglobin <9.0 g/dL or 5.6 mmol/L Note: Criteria must be met without transfusion or growth factors within last 2 weeks.
